seo_title: RBI Issues Domestic Money Transfer Directions, 2026
title: RBI Consolidates Domestic Money Transfer Rules Into One 2026 Direction
case_name: Reserve Bank of India (Domestic Money Transfer) Directions, 2026
citation: RBI/DPSS/2026-27/476, dated 11 November 2026, issued under Section 18 read with Section 10(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007
card_summary: The Reserve Bank of India issued the Domestic Money Transfer Directions, 2026 on 11 November 2026, replacing its 2011 and 2024 circulars with one framework. Transfers must run in near real time, with inter-bank settlement through RBI-approved systems only. Banks must record the remitter's details and a cash-remittance identifier on IMPS/NEFT messages for unbanked customers; card-to-card transfers are excluded.
card_tip: A bank handling a cash-based IMPS or NEFT remittance for someone without an account must now capture the remitter's identity and a remittance identifier; card-to-card transfers are not covered by these Directions.
verification_notes: AUDIENCE: domestic (banks, remittance customers, migrant workers sending cash home), with a secondary NRI angle for family members in India receiving domestic transfers from relatives abroad who then move funds onward. TARGET QUERY: new RBI rules for sending money by NEFT IMPS 2026. DEMAND EVIDENCE: none seen. Cross-verified across the RBI's own notification text, TaxGuru's summary and the All India Radio (Newsonair) report, which agree on the Directions' number (RBI/DPSS/2026-27/476), the 11 November 2026 date, the statutory basis (Section 18 read with Section 10(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007), the near-real-time settlement requirement, the remitter-detail and cash-remittance-identifier requirement for unbanked customers, the repeal of the 2011 and 2024 circulars, and the carve-out for card-to-card transfers. A secondary report (Sarkaritel) states the cash-based NEFT remittance cap stayed at Rs 50,000, but this figure could not be confirmed against the RBI's own text in this run, so it is left out of the card above.
